AIRM-401: Remote session list has no done/all/active filter
body.description:
YouTrack: [AIRM-401](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/AIRM-401)
Related: [air-mobile #627](https://github.com/JetBrains/air-mobile/pull/627), [air-ahp-extensions #16](https://github.com/JetBrains/air-ahp-extensions/pull/16)

## What and why

Air mobile can mark a Remote Control session Done but could never see Done sessions: `isExposableToMobile` excluded archived sessions, so a Done session vanished with `root/sessionRemoved`. The phone now gets an Active / Done / All filter like the desktop session list (air-mobile #627), and this change makes the host serve what it needs.

- **Done sessions are served** in `listSessions` / `root/sessionAdded` with AHP's standard `SessionStatus` bit `IsArchived` (64). Status follows the AHP aggregation rule (activity bits from the chats, `IsRead` / `IsArchived` session-scoped); no IDLE is forced. Every value passes `isProducerLegal`.
- **Mark as Done follows the AHP spec.** AHP says `session/isArchivedChanged` is "Dispatched by a client to archive a session ... or to unarchive it", and `session/dispose` removes a session. The host now accepts a client `session/isArchivedChanged {isArchived: true}` on a listed session as Mark as Done, through the IDE's own archive path (`AgentThreadArchiveService`, a running turn is stopped first). The echo wait is bounded at 12 s (below the phone's 15 s); the archive keeps running after the bound. A session already done is applied with no IDE call; a dropped duplicate waits for the running archive of that row (`AgentThreadArchiveService.awaitRunningArchive`). A draft is refused (`DRAFT_NOT_DONE`).
- **Reopen:** `{isArchived: false}` reopens, as the desktop's explicit open of a Done row does (IJPL-244497, `resolveArchivedThreadOpen`), through `unarchiveOnOpenInBackground` with the same 12 s bound.
- **`session/dispose`:** a draft is disposed for real. Any other session is refused with `PermissionDenied` (-32009), "this host does not dispose a session; mark it done with session/isArchivedChanged": AHP's dispose removes a session and IJ Air has no session delete. The old archive-on-dispose path and the leg's dispose lock are deleted. A phone that stops a published session marks it done instead.
- **Archiving and reopening** (desktop or phone) send `root/sessionSummaryChanged` with the new status and `session/isArchivedChanged` on the session channel, never `root/sessionRemoved`.
- **A Done session takes no new message**, as on the desktop (`chat/turnStarted` and `chat/pendingMessageSet` are refused).
- **Active-only consumers stay active-only:** attention, push and the ACP surface read `servedSessions()`; `activeSessions` counts only active sessions.

## Decisions for the reviewer

- **Cost.** The Done set only grows, so no path replays the log of a Done session no device follows. Active and Done come from one read of each project's log (`AirAhpServedSession.Active` / `Done`); a Done session is read from its compact summary (`listProjection`). A push batch reads the followed sessions once and pushes only followed sessions. A `listSessions` walk is ordered once per leg (cursor `s:<n>`), and each page reads only its own rows. Session lookups by uuid are memoized and re-checked with one summary read (`exposureOf`), which is also the one owner of "is this session done".
- **What remains per batch:** the exposure scan and an O(done) compact read per push batch. Master already walked every log thread, archived ones included, once per batch, so this is a constant-factor increase; removing it needs an incremental exposure index.
- **Phone compatibility:** air-mobile #627 marks done only with `session/isArchivedChanged`, with no fallback, by decision. A phone built before #627 cannot mark a session done against this host (its dispose is refused), and a phone with #627 against an IDE without this change shows that host's refusal.
- **Landing order:** air-mobile #627 must land first. An older phone ignores the `IsArchived` bit and would show every Done session among the active ones. A phone with #627 against an older host simply shows an empty Done view.
- **Not done:** a Done entry's `createdAt` is its list order time, because the compact summary keeps no creation time (fixing that touches `session.projection`); a Done session whose last turn failed still lists idle in the catalogue (97 when read), because the compact `summary.json` row records no turn failure; the subscribed session state reports it correctly (98). A Mark as Done does not clear the `activity` a device holds, because AHP has no value that clears it (the phone does not read it for these rows). A duplicate done mark dropped in the short window before the running archive is registered gets a refusal although the session then becomes done; the device sees it done through the summary change. One Patronus failure (`GoCodeStyleSettings` IdeException in IDEA Product Tests) is in the Go plugin, which this change does not touch. The worker chat or task of a Done session resolves after an IDE restart once a leg follows that session.

## Verification

- `bt plugins/air/backend/mobile` (both targets): 2051 tests passed.
- `bt plugins/air/backend/session/runtime`: 2938 tests passed (`AgentThreadArchiveService`, `AgentThreadLaunchService` touched).
- `AirSpecReferencesTest`, jscpd: green. Specs updated: `mobile-ahp-host.spec.md`, `mobile-exposure-filter.spec.md`, `mobile-session-actions.spec.md`.
- Each new test was mutation-checked (the guard removed, the test fails, restored).
- Six review rounds, plus two on the Mark as Done change; the last ones found nothing major or worse.

No visual change.

IJAI-5507: Flaky AirMobileIdeSessionActionsTest: a session deleted during a follow-up wait ends the delivery quietly
body.description:
YouTrack: [IJAI-5507](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IJAI-5507)

## What and why

`AirMobileIdeSessionActionsTest.aPhoneQueuedMessageAddedWhileIdleReleasesTheHoldOfAFailedTurn` flaked on TeamCity ([build 1112815591](https://buildserver.labs.intellij.net/build/1112815591)). Its assertions passed, and it then failed in `afterEach` on an uncaught `IllegalStateException: The session loop command lost a cancellation` from the `FollowUpDeliveryCoordinator` coroutine.

Root cause: `FollowUpCommandBoundary` records a follow-up event and then waits until it is applied. The production port waited with `SessionProjectionApplier.awaitSeq`. When the session is deleted during that wait (in the test, by the `@AfterEach` purge), `awaitSeq` throws `CancellationException("The session ... closed")`. The boundary's worker is still active, so `SessionLoopRequest.run` correctly reports that foreign cancellation as "lost". The exception leaves the queue pass, and nothing catches it.

Fix:
- `SessionProjectionStore.awaitSeqOrClosed(threadId, seq): SessionApplyWait` is the per-event twin of the existing `awaitAppendedOrClosed`. `ProjectedSessionEventStore` implements it on the applier's `awaitApplied`, and `awaitAppendedOrClosed` now delegates to it. On a store that is already closed it answers `Closed`, which is what `awaitAppendedOrClosed`'s KDoc already promised.
- `SessionLogFollowUpEventAccess.awaitApplied` uses the closed-aware wait. After a delete, the boundary's next read shows the deleted session's empty state, so the command ends as not applied, and the delivery ends with no failure. `SessionLoopRequest` is unchanged.
- Test helper fix: `holdApplier` in `SessionProjectionTestSupport.kt` returned before the applier was actually held, so a later pull could apply the next appends and the hold held nothing. It now returns only once the applier waits at the hold. Its six other callers only get stricter holds.

## Decisions

- Scope is the reported race: a session deleted while a follow-up command waits for its own event. A projection store that closes during the wait or before the command starts, and a store service disposed between the record and the wait, still produce the same exception. They are left for a follow-up issue. A close or purge drains the tail first, so the wait answers `Applied` and the next read throws. Replacing a store between the record and the wait is safe.
- An earlier iteration added a `Closed` branch in the boundary for a closed store. It was removed because production cannot reach it: the port looks up the store again on every call.
- Known and left open: `applied = false` also covers "session deleted". After a delete, enqueue answers `DuplicateId`, and reorder and `setPauseAfter` report success. Before this change, those callers got the uncaught `IllegalStateException`.

## Verification

- New test `FollowUpQueueTurnBoundaryTest#a session deleted while the outcome of a delivery is recorded ends the delivery quietly`. It goes through the production port and store. The applier is held, the wait registers with `UNDISPATCHED`, and the session is then deleted. No timing and no loops. It passes 10 of 10 runs (`--runs_per_test=10`). With the port reverted to `awaitSeq` it fails with the TeamCity stack ("lost a cancellation" at `SessionCommandLoop.kt:185`).
- New store tests in `SessionProjectionApplierTest`: a deleted session, and a closed store, each end the wait as closed.
- Uncached and green: `FollowUpDeliveryCoordinatorTest` (148), `FollowUpDeliveryCoordinatorBusTest`, `FollowUpQueueTurnBoundaryTest`, `SessionProjectionApplierTest`, `AirMobileIdeSessionActionsTest` (58), `SessionCommandLoopTest`, `AirSpecReferencesTest`, `ClosedProjectionStoreTest`, the `backend/session/projection` subtree (829), and `BT build //plugins/air/...`.
- `--lane fast` on the first iteration: 7 failures, in `frontend/llm` (`AirAiAccessSettingsConfigurableTest`) and `backend/nextEdits/acp` (`AcpNextEdit*E2ETest` timeouts). `bazel query somepath` shows no path from either target to a changed module. These failures were not checked on clean master.
- Four review rounds by independent reviewers. The last round reported no major-or-worse findings.

No visual change.
